course_description:
This course applies a strategic social marketing approach to identify and examine wicked social problems. In practice, social marketing seeks to integrate marketing concepts, with other approaches to influence behaviour change that benefit individuals, communities and wider society for social good. Social marketing is guided by ethical principles, integrates research insight, advances theory as a lens to understand consumers and other stakeholders, and applies marketing techniques and strategies to influence social change at micro, meso and macro levels of society.

In this course instance, students will use human-centred design to develop practical, evidence-informed social change solutions. Working with a social change partner, students will apply social marketing concepts to a current behaviour change challenge and pitch a campaign designed to support positive social outcomes.

Sustainable Development Goals - UQ Business School is a proud supporter and Advanced Signatory of the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (UN PRME) . As part of the largest global collaboration between business schools and the UN, the school emphasises its role in empowering students to drive societal transformation through the Sustainable Development Goals . The SDGs highlight that a thriving economy relies on a healthy environment, aiming to balance economic growth, social well-being, and environmental protection for a sustainable future.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

In response to student feedback, the course has replaced separate weekly tutorial worksheets with a Social Marketing Strategy Workbook. The workbook supports students to progressively document, review and refine their social change ideas, research insights and application of social marketing concepts as they develop their project across the semester.

The course will:

learning_outcomes.description: Interpret and apply social marketing principles and techniques to influence positive behaviour change.
Describe and distinguish the commonly used behavioural change theories in social marketing.
Analyse societal problems for relevant ethical and socially responsible marketing solutions.
Plan, conduct and present secondary and primary research appropriate for a specific social behaviour change enquiry.
Demonstrate effective communication and collaboration abilities in making social innovation decisions as a group.

assessment_details.title: Social Change Project - Part A - Social Marketing Insights and Targeting Report
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessment factor. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Students will form a team of FIVE students from their tutorial class to develop an evidence-informed behaviour change strategy using social marketing, behavioural theory and human-centred design. In Part A, teams will investigate the social issue, map key stakeholders and segment potential audiences before selecting a priority target market. They will then develop an evidence-informed persona that captures the audience’s behaviours, needs, motivations and barriers. These insights will guide the social marketing strategy presented in Part B. assessment_details.task_description: Team Social Marketing Strategy Pitch - Group Mark 25% Building on the insights from Part A, the same team as Part A, will deliver a 20-minute oral presentation (including 5 min Q&A) that outlines their proposed social marketing strategy to peers and tutors during scheduled Week 12 sessions. The presentation will be guided by the design thinking process and must demonstrate the team’s ability to apply social marketing theory, communicate behavioural insights, and justify their strategic approach. Presentation Requirements: All team members must participate in the presentation. Presentations will be assessed on both content and delivery. Presentation times will be scheduled in-class during Week 12. Teamwork and Peer Assessment: Effective teamwork is essential for the success of this project. All teams must complete a team contract to guide team operations (a template will be provided). Peer contribution will be assessed using Buddycheck , the UQ group peer assessment tool available on Blackboard. Students whose contributions are assessed as significantly below that of their peers may receive a reduced mark. Peer assessments must be submitted by the end of the day following your team’s presentation. If you experience issues within your team, it is important to notify your tutor as early as possible. Students are encouraged to complete the online edX course “Working in Teams: A Practical Guide” to support effective team functioning. A link to this resource is available on Blackboard. Please Note: The presentation will be recorded for marking purposes per UQ Policy. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Social Marketing Strategy Justification and Evaluation Report
assessment_details.task_description: In the final managerial report students will critically justify and evaluate their team’s proposed social marketing strategy against the social marketing benchmark criteria. The individual report will assess key strategic decisions, propose an evaluation framework for measuring implementation and behaviour change outcomes, and examine relevant ethical considerations. Students must demonstrate how the strategy can achieve effective, responsible and accountable social change. Report requirements: The 1500 words (+/- 10%) report will be written in report style, including an Executive Summary, appendices of information and tables (not included in the word count).
